9. Mission Lifecycle

DRAFTSUBMITTEDAPPROVEDACTIVECOMPLETEDREJECTEDCANCELLED

stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> DRAFT : create (lead/director) DRAFT --> SUBMITTED : submit\n[≥1 requirement] SUBMITTED --> APPROVED : approve\n[director OR non-creator lead] SUBMITTED --> REJECTED : reject + reason REJECTED --> DRAFT : revise APPROVED --> ACTIVE : activate\n[all slots ACCEPTED] APPROVED --> DRAFT : amend\n[re-approval required] ACTIVE --> COMPLETED : complete DRAFT --> CANCELLED : cancel SUBMITTED --> CANCELLED : cancel APPROVED --> CANCELLED : cancel COMPLETED --> [*] CANCELLED --> [*]
TransitionActorGuard (enforced in service, transactional)
create → DRAFTLead+valid window (start < end), title required
DRAFT → SUBMITTEDLead+ (creator)≥1 skill requirement; every requirement headcount ≥ 1; submission_count += 1
SUBMITTED → APPROVEDDirector, or Lead where actor ≠ created_byrecords approved_by; offers already OFFERED remain valid
SUBMITTED → REJECTEDsame as approverejection_reason mandatory
REJECTED → DRAFTcreatorunlocks editing; history preserved in events
APPROVED → ACTIVELead+every requirement's ACCEPTED count ≥ headcount; error lists the gaps otherwise
APPROVED → DRAFT (amend)Lead+material changes only; ACCEPTED assignments retained; must re-pass approval before activation
ACTIVE → COMPLETEDLead+—
any non-terminal → CANCELLEDLead+open offers → WITHDRAWN in same transaction

Editing a mission's fields/requirements is only possible in DRAFT. SUBMITTED is read-only pending decision — this is what makes approval meaningful.

10. Assignment Lifecycle

stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> OFFERED : matcher offer (lead) OFFERED --> ACCEPTED : crew accepts OFFERED --> DECLINED : crew declines + reason OFFERED --> WITHDRAWN : lead withdraws / mission cancelled ACCEPTED --> WITHDRAWN : crew drops out DECLINED --> [*] : triggers top-up match WITHDRAWN --> [*] : triggers backfill match
  • Offers are created in waves: the matcher returns ranked candidates; the lead offers the top k per slot (primary + named backups). Backups are explicit offers, not a hidden queue — crew see exactly what they're being offered.
  • Accept/decline is idempotent: only OFFERED → terminal transitions allowed; anything else → 409. Response recorded with responded_at and reason.
  • A slot is open when ACCEPTED count < requirement.headcount — a derived value, never stored, so it can't drift.

11. Matching Engine

flowchart TD A["Mission requirements
(skill, min proficiency, headcount) + window"] --> B subgraph B["Hard filters (SQL, org-scoped)"] F1["1. Same org (tenant scope)"] F2["2. Holds ALL required skills
at proficiency ≥ min"] F3["3. No UNAVAILABLE window
overlapping mission window"] F4["4. No ACCEPTED assignment on
overlapping mission"] F5["5. Under workload cap
(≤ 2 concurrent missions)"] F6["6. Not already DECLINED/WITHDRAWN
for this mission (top-up mode)"] F1 --> F2 --> F3 --> F4 --> F5 --> F6 end B --> C["Score survivors (app code, deterministic)"] C --> D["Rank + per-criterion breakdown"] D --> E["Primary = top headcount
Backups = next N"] D --> F["If empty: report which filter
eliminated how many"]

Scoring (weights are named constants, tunable in one place)

score = 0.40 · skillFit + 0.25 · workload + 0.20 · experience + 0.15 · reliability

skillFit     = avg over required skills of (proficiency / 5)
workload     = 1 − (committed mission-days in window / window days)    ∈ [0,1]
experience  = min(1, relevant completed missions / 5)
reliability = 1 − (lifetime declines / lifetime offers)    (new crew = 1.0)

Tie-break: higher skillFit → lower committed days → stable id order. Fully deterministic: same inputs, same ranking, every time.

Worked example

Mission "Europa Survey" requires Orbital Navigation ≥ 4 and EVA Ops ≥ 3, window 2026-11-01 → 2026-11-30 (30 days), headcount 1 per skill.

CandidateskillFitworkloadexperiencereliabilityScore
Crew A — Nav 5, EVA 4; 0 committed days; 3 past missions; 0/2 declines0.901.000.601.000.880
Crew B — Nav 4, EVA 3; 10 committed days; 5 past missions; 1/5 declines0.700.671.000.800.768

Crew A is offered primary; Crew B is the named backup. If A declines, top-up re-runs excluding A and offers B — no manual cross-referencing.

Failure reporting

When no candidate survives, the matcher returns the elimination funnel — e.g. { skillBar: 9, availability: 2, conflicts: 1, survivors: 0 } — so the lead knows whether to lower the bar, shift the window, or split the requirement. Explainability includes explaining failure.

12. Edge Cases

12.1 Mission rejected → revision loop

REJECTED carries a mandatory reason; revise returns the mission to DRAFT with full history intact. Resubmission increments submission_count; the approver sees prior rejection reasons in the audit trail. No data is lost across the loop.

12.2 Crew declines an offer → substitute wave

The DECLINED row persists (exclusion + reliability input). Top-up matching re-runs with the declined user excluded and offers the next-ranked candidate for that specific slot. The mission itself is untouched.

12.3 Crew drops out after approval → least-disruption backfill

Assignment → WITHDRAWN. The mission stays APPROVED/ACTIVE; only the vacated slot re-opens (derived: ACCEPTED < headcount). Backfill offers for that slot do not require re-approval — the plan was already approved; a personnel swap within it is operations, not policy. Escalation path: if backfill finds no candidates, the lead amends the mission (APPROVED → DRAFT), which does force re-approval — material change, not a personnel swap.

12.4 Also handled

  • No eligible candidates: elimination funnel returned (§11), never a silent empty list.
  • Double response: second accept/decline → 409 (idempotency).
  • Mission cancelled with live offers: all OFFERED → WITHDRAWN in the same transaction.
  • Approval of own mission by a lead: 403 with explicit reason code CANNOT_APPROVE_OWN.
  • Cross-tenant access by ID guessing: org filter + cuid IDs → 404 (not 403 — don't confirm existence).
  • Activation with open slots: 422 listing exactly which requirements are under-filled.

13. API Surface

Base: /v1 · Auth: Authorization: Bearer <token> · Errors: { error: { code, message, details? } } with consistent codes.

EndpointRolePurpose
GET /v1/meanyIdentity, org, role
GET|POST /v1/skills · DELETE /v1/skills/:idread: lead+ · write: directorOrg skill taxonomy
GET /v1/crew · GET /v1/crew/:idlead+ (crew: self)Directory with skills/availability
PUT /v1/me/skillsanyReplace own skill ratings
POST|GET /v1/me/availability · DELETE /v1/me/availability/:idanyOwn unavailable windows
POST /v1/missions · GET /v1/missions · GET /v1/missions/:id · PATCH /v1/missions/:idlead+ (crew: assigned only)CRUD; PATCH only in DRAFT
PUT /v1/missions/:id/requirementslead+Replace requirement set (DRAFT only)
POST /v1/missions/:id/submit | approve | reject | activate | complete | cancel | reviseper §9 guardsLifecycle transitions
POST /v1/missions/:id/matchlead+Run matcher → ranked candidates + breakdown (dry run)
POST /v1/missions/:id/offerslead+Create offers from a match result (wave)
GET /v1/me/offersanyMy pending/responded offers
POST /v1/assignments/:id/accept | decline | withdrawoffer owner (withdraw: lead+)Respond / drop out
GET /v1/missions/:id/eventslead+ (crew: if assigned)Audit trail

14. CLI

Binary mc. Config (token + API URL) in ~/.mission-control/config.json via mc login --token …. Every command supports --json; human output is aligned tables. Non-zero exit codes on failure; errors print code: message.

mc login --token <token> [--api http://localhost:3000]
mc whoami

mc skills list | add <name> | remove <id>              # director for writes
mc crew list | show <id>

mc profile skills set <skill> <1-5> [...]
mc profile availability add <start> <end> [--note …]
mc profile availability list | remove <id>

mc missions create --title … --start … --end …
mc missions requirements set <id> --skill <name>:<min>:<count> [...]
mc missions list [--status …] | show <id> | history <id>
mc missions submit <id> | approve <id> | reject <id> --reason …
mc missions activate <id> | complete <id> | cancel <id> | revise <id>

mc missions match <id> [--top-up]             # ranked table + breakdown
mc missions offer <id> --crew <id> [...]      # send offer wave

mc offers list                                  # the crew member's inbox
mc offers accept <assignmentId>
mc offers decline <assignmentId> --reason …
mc offers withdraw <assignmentId>              # drop out post-acceptance

The demo script (README) walks: seed → lead builds mission → match → offer → submit → second lead approves → crew accepts → activate → dropout → top-up backfill → complete.

15. Seed Data

  • Two orgs — "Astra Dynamics" and "Lunar Collective" — with different skill taxonomies (e.g. Orbital Navigation/EVA Ops vs Regolith Assay/Life Support) to prove per-org scoping.
  • Per org: 1 director, 2 mission leads, 8 crew with varied proficiencies, overlapping unavailable windows, and assignment history (completed missions feed the experience score).
  • Missions pre-seeded in DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED and ACTIVE states so every CLI command has something to act on immediately.
  • One seeded crew member with a decline history (reliability < 1) so score differences are visible in the demo.
  • Printed token table on npm run seed — one line per user, copy-paste into mc login.

16. Verification Plan

LayerTests (Vitest)
Matcher (unit)Each hard filter in isolation; scoring formula against hand-computed values; tie-break determinism; empty-result funnel counts; top-up exclusions.
State machine (unit)Every legal transition passes; every illegal one rejects (incl. lead-approves-own → 403); cancel withdraws offers transactionally.
RBAC (integration)Each endpoint × each role → expected allow/deny matrix from §7.
Tenancy (integration)Org A token cannot read/mutate any Org B resource by ID (404), cannot list across tenants, matcher never suggests cross-tenant crew.
Workflow (integration)Full happy path end-to-end; decline→top-up; post-approval dropout→backfill; reject→revise→resubmit→approve.
CLI (smoke)Each command against a live local server: exit codes + --json parseability.

17. Extension Points (designed for, not built)

  • Resource/equipment constraints: new resources + mission_resource_requirements tables; matcher gains a hard filter and the score a weight — no schema upheaval. (Anticipated live-session question.)
  • Per-org approval chains: organizations.settings.approval_policy (e.g. two-director sign-off, auto-approve under N crew) evaluated in the approve guard.
  • Multi-org users: split users into global users + memberships(user_id, org_id, role); auth context already carries (user, org, role) as a tuple.
  • Postgres/GCP: Prisma datasource swap; Cloud SQL + Cloud Run is the natural deployment.
  • Notifications: an outbox row per offer event; a worker delivers email/webhooks. CLI polling remains the fallback.

18. Time Plan (3–5h budget)

BlockScopeBudget
1This design document0:30
2Repo scaffold, Prisma schema, migrations, seed0:45
3API: auth, RBAC, crew/skills, mission CRUD + lifecycle1:00
4Matcher + offers + assignment responses0:30
5CLI full command tree0:30
6Tests (matcher, state machine, RBAC, tenancy, workflow)0:45
7README (setup + demo script), commit hygiene, transcript export0:30

// so status/role/kind fields are String (validated by zod + TS unions at the

  provider = "sqlite"
  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")
}

generator client {
  provider = "prisma-client-js"
}

model Organization {
  id        String         @id @default(cuid())
  name      String
  slug      String         @unique
  settings  String         @default("{}") // JSON: e.g. approval_policy (extension point)
  createdAt DateTime       @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  users     User[]
  skills    Skill[]
  missions  Mission[]
  events    MissionEvent[]

  @@map("organizations")
}

model User {
  id               String               @id @default(cuid())
  orgId            String               @map("org_id")
  name             String
  email            String               @unique
  role             String               // DIRECTOR | MISSION_LEAD | CREW_MEMBER
  apiKey           String               @unique @map("api_key")
  createdAt        DateTime             @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  org              Organization         @relation(fields: [orgId], references: [id])
  crewSkills       CrewSkill[]
  availability     AvailabilityWindow[]
  assignments      Assignment[]
  createdMissions  Mission[]            @relation("MissionCreator")
  approvedMissions Mission[]            @relation("MissionApprover")
  events           MissionEvent[]

  @@index([orgId])
  @@map("users")
}

model Skill {
  id          String                    @id @default(cuid())
  orgId       String                    @map("org_id")
  name        String
  description String?
  org         Organization              @relation(fields: [orgId], references: [id])
  crewSkills  CrewSkill[]
  requirements MissionSkillRequirement[]

  @@unique([orgId, name])
  @@map("skills")
}

model CrewSkill {
  userId      String @map("user_id")
  skillId     String @map("skill_id")
  proficiency Int // 1-5
  user        User   @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id])
  skill       Skill  @relation(fields: [skillId], references: [id])

  @@id([userId, skillId])
  @@index([skillId, proficiency])
  @@map("crew_skills")
}

model AvailabilityWindow {
  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
  userId    String   @map("user_id")
  startDate DateTime @map("start_date") // date-only semantics (UTC midnight)
  endDate   DateTime @map("end_date")
  kind      String   @default("UNAVAILABLE") // UNAVAILABLE (leave, training, ...)
  note      String?
  user      User     @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id])

  @@index([userId, startDate, endDate])
  @@map("availability_windows")
}

model Mission {
  id              String                    @id @default(cuid())
  orgId           String                    @map("org_id")
  title           String
  description     String?
  startDate       DateTime                  @map("start_date")
  endDate         DateTime                  @map("end_date")
  status          String                    @default("DRAFT") // DRAFT|SUBMITTED|APPROVED|ACTIVE|COMPLETED|REJECTED|CANCELLED
  createdBy       String                    @map("created_by")
  approvedBy      String?                   @map("approved_by")
  rejectionReason String?                   @map("rejection_reason")
  submissionCount Int                       @default(0) @map("submission_count")
  createdAt       DateTime                  @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt       DateTime                  @updatedAt @map("updated_at")
  org             Organization              @relation(fields: [orgId], references: [id])
  creator         User                      @relation("MissionCreator", fields: [createdBy], references: [id])
  approver        User?                     @relation("MissionApprover", fields: [approvedBy], references: [id])
  requirements    MissionSkillRequirement[]
  assignments     Assignment[]
  events          MissionEvent[]

  @@index([orgId, status])
  @@map("missions")
}

model MissionSkillRequirement {
  id             String       @id @default(cuid())
  missionId      String       @map("mission_id")
  skillId        String       @map("skill_id")
  minProficiency Int          @map("min_proficiency") // 1-5
  headcount      Int // slots to fill for this skill
  mission        Mission      @relation(fields: [missionId], references: [id])
  skill          Skill        @relation(fields: [skillId], references: [id])
  assignments    Assignment[]

  @@unique([missionId, skillId])
  @@map("mission_skill_requirements")
}

model Assignment {
  id             String                  @id @default(cuid())
  missionId      String                  @map("mission_id")
  requirementId  String                  @map("requirement_id")
  userId         String                  @map("user_id")
  status         String                  @default("OFFERED") // OFFERED|ACCEPTED|DECLINED|WITHDRAWN
  matchScore     Float                   @map("match_score")
  scoreBreakdown String                  @map("score_breakdown") // JSON: per-criterion scores
  declineReason  String?                 @map("decline_reason")
  offeredAt      DateTime                @default(now()) @map("offered_at")
  respondedAt    DateTime?               @map("responded_at")
  mission        Mission                 @relation(fields: [missionId], references: [id])
  requirement    MissionSkillRequirement @relation(fields: [requirementId], references: [id])
  user           User                    @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id])

  @@index([missionId, status])
  @@index([userId, status])
  @@map("assignments")
}

model MissionEvent {
  id         String       @id @default(cuid())
  orgId      String       @map("org_id")
  missionId  String       @map("mission_id")
  actorId    String       @map("actor_id")
  eventType  String       @map("event_type") // CREATED|SUBMITTED|APPROVED|REJECTED|ACTIVATED|COMPLETED|CANCELLED|REVISED|OFFERED|ACCEPTED|DECLINED|WITHDRAWN|BACKFILLED
  fromStatus String?      @map("from_status")
  toStatus   String?      @map("to_status")
  payload    String       @default("{}") // JSON: reason, score, slot, ...
  createdAt  DateTime     @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  org        Organization @relation(fields: [orgId], references: [id])
  mission    Mission      @relation(fields: [missionId], references: [id])
  actor      User         @relation(fields: [actorId], references: [id])

  @@index([missionId])
  @@index([orgId])
  @@map("mission_events")
}

content.text:
My overall take: this already reads like a senior design doc. The decision log with rejected alternatives, the "why nobody matched" breakdown, slot-level repair (D7), returning 404 instead of 403 across tenants, storing the score breakdown on every offer, and keeping the CLI free of business logic are the signals the brief is looking for. The problems are a few internal contradictions an agent would resolve by guessing, one requirement the brief states that the doc postpones, and some process gaps.

**Heads-up first:** a [schema.prisma](C:/Users/shubh/OneDrive/Documents/Mutinex/mission-control/prisma/schema.prisma) appeared at 18:46 while I was reading, and packages are being installed. If another session is building, I'd pause it until the design settles, because the schema already locks in issues 1 and 3 below. Also, there's no git repo yet.

## 1. Contradictions to fix before any code

1. **One person per skill, or one person with all the skills?** Filter F2 says a candidate must hold *all* required skills ([design.html:394](C:/Users/shubh/OneDrive/Documents/Mutinex/design.html:394)). The worked example has one person covering both skills, with "A primary, B backup". But the data model gives each skill its own headcount, and each assignment points at one requirement. With headcount 1 per skill, A should fill one slot and B the other.
   - **Fix:** model *roles*: `mission_roles(name, headcount)` plus `role_skill_requirements`. "Pilot ×1 needs Nav≥4 and EVA≥2" covers both readings, and it's how real crews work (Commander, Pilot, Flight Engineer).
   - **Then matching becomes an assignment problem**, and filling each slot greedily fails. Example: A qualifies for Pilot and Engineer and ranks top in both; B only qualifies for Pilot. Greedy puts A in Pilot and leaves Engineer empty. Either fill the hardest-to-staff role first, or use Hungarian matching that fills the most slots first and then maximises total score. This is where "sophistication of the algorithm" gets judged.

2. **The workload score never changes anything.** F4 already removes anyone with an accepted mission overlapping the window. So for everyone left, "committed days in window" is always 0, workload is always 1.0, and its 25% weight does nothing. F5's "≤2 concurrent missions" can't trigger either, unless pending offers count, which the doc doesn't say. Crew B in the worked example (10 committed days) would have been filtered out. **Fix:** treat missions as exclusive (F4), measure workload over a wider horizon such as ±90 days, and optionally add a minimum rest gap between missions as an org setting.

3. **When can offers be sent?** The demo script sends offers in DRAFT, before approval ([design.html:502](C:/Users/shubh/OneDrive/Documents/Mutinex/design.html:502)). That means crew can accept a mission that later gets rejected. It also means `PUT /requirements` (replace the whole set) leaves orphaned offers, since each assignment links to a requirement row. **Fix:** allow the matcher's dry run at any time, but only send offers once a mission is APPROVED. Save a snapshot at submit time showing the mission can be staffed, so the approver knows it's viable. Requirements are then locked before any offer exists, and the orphan problem disappears.

4. **Lifecycle gaps:**
   - ACTIVE → CANCELLED is missing from the diagram, although the table says "any non-terminal state can be cancelled" (line 367).
   - Cancel from REJECTED is missing.
   - There's no way for a lead to withdraw a submission (SUBMITTED → DRAFT).
   - Amending the dates must re-check that accepted crew are still available.

5. **Backup offers can overfill a slot.** If the primary and the backup both accept, the slot has too many people. Offer exactly the headcount, show backups to the lead as a ranked bench, and reject any accept once the slot is full (a `SLOT_FILLED` error).

6. **Crew can be double-booked.** Pending offers don't block other offers, so someone can accept two overlapping missions. Accepting must re-check conflicts and availability in the same transaction, then automatically withdraw that person's other overlapping pending offers. Also decide what happens when crew add leave that overlaps a mission they've accepted.

## 2. Cheap changes that map straight onto the brief

7. **Different approval processes per org.** The brief says orgs have "different… approval processes", and the doc postpones that. Build a small per-org policy: which roles can approve, how many approvals are needed, no self-approval. Add a `mission_approvals` table (approver, revision, decision, snapshot). Seed Org A with peer-lead approval (your D5) and Org B with director-only approval. That turns the D5 ambiguity into a feature, gives directors real "settings" (the brief says they manage settings, but there's no settings endpoint yet), and prepares you for the live question about redesigning approval workflows. Also, directors can currently approve their own missions; I'd make "nobody approves their own mission" a universal rule.

8. **Crew rate their own skills.** With `PUT /me/skills`, anyone can rate themselves 5 in everything and game the matcher. Let crew self-assess, have leads or directors verify, and have the matcher use only verified ratings (or flag unverified ones). An optional `expires_at` on certifications (EVA qualifications, medicals) as a hard filter is cheap and very true to the domain.

9. **The reliability score is unfair.** It penalises legitimate declines, and one decline out of one offer scores 0. I'd measure dropouts *after* accepting (the thing that actually disrupts a mission), smooth it so a few data points can't swing it, and give it a small weight. Or drop it. Crew shouldn't see anyone else's breakdown.

10. **Enforce tenancy in the database.** The ER diagram says `org_id` is on every table, but crew skills, availability, requirements and assignments don't have it. Nothing stops an org-A user being linked to an org-B skill through API input. Composite foreign keys on `(org_id, id)` make that impossible. Tests should also try foreign IDs in request bodies, not just GET by ID. Hashing tokens takes about three lines, so do it now rather than listing it as hardening.

11. **Make the matcher a pure function over an in-memory snapshot, not SQL filters.** Counting eliminations per filter, "why not Alice?", and near misses ("nobody has EVA≥4, but 3 crew have EVA 3") become trivial, and unit tests don't need a database.

12. **Write the rules once, as data.** A transition table (from, action, to, guard) plus a permission map can drive enforcement, an `allowedActions` field in API responses, and table-driven tests. Use conditional updates (`WHERE status = 'SUBMITTED'`) so two people approving at once can't both succeed.

## 3. CLI usability (explicitly assessed)

- **Human-readable IDs:** per-org `MSN-12`, crew by handle, skills by name. Nobody wants to type cuids.
- **Profile switching:** reviewers will jump between director, lead and crew constantly. Support something like `mc use lead-astra`, and have the seed script print ready-to-paste login commands.
- **`mc inbox`** that depends on your role: approvals waiting (director), declined slots to refill (lead), pending offers (crew).
- **`mc missions show`:** staffing per role (e.g. 2/3), what's blocking activation, and "actions available to you" from the server's `allowedActions`.
- **Matching:** `match --explain <crew>` for why or why not, and `offer MSN-3 --recommended` instead of pasting IDs.
- **Polish:** next-step hints after each command, errors that say what to do, documented exit codes.
- **`npm run demo`:** a scripted walkthrough that is both a convenience for reviewers and smoke-test evidence.

## 4. Process and packaging

- **Git:** run `git init` now and make the first commit the brief plus the design doc, so the history proves the design came first. Revising the doc *now* is fine and looks good in the transcript. Once coding starts, keep a log of where you diverged instead of rewriting the doc; the live session asks about exactly that.
- **Format:** GitHub shows `design.html` as raw source. Make a `docs/DESIGN.md` the main copy, since GitHub renders mermaid diagrams natively.
- **A `CLAUDE.md` for the agent** would be your strongest evidence of "directing an agent". It should hold:
  - the commands and folder layout;
  - the invariants ("every repository function takes `orgId` first", "never take `orgId` from the request", "transitions only through the table");
  - a definition of done for each milestone.
- **Scope:** 7 mission states, ~25 endpoints, ~25 CLI commands and 6 test layers is a lot for 3–5 hours, and the brief favours a vertical slice over breadth. Mark Must/Should/Could so the agent knows what to drop (e.g. the amend flow is a Could).
- **Date rules:** state that ranges are inclusive, give the overlap test, and say dates are UTC. Agents often get off-by-one errors here.
- **Dependencies:**
  - `package.json` has no devDependencies (Prisma CLI, TypeScript, tsx, Vitest) and no `bin` entry for `mc`, so the scripts won't run as written.
  - Prisma 7.10 is installed, but the schema uses older syntax (`url = env(...)`, `prisma-client-js`, lines 8 and 12). As far as I know, Prisma 7 moved the connection URL into `prisma.config.ts`, needs a driver adapter for SQLite, and no longer loads `.env` automatically; I couldn't confirm this from the installed files. Either pin Prisma 6 or write the Prisma 7 specifics into `CLAUDE.md`.
  - The schema comment says SQLite has no enums or JSON columns in Prisma. I believe support for both arrived in 6.2, which is worth checking.

## If you only change five things

1. The roles model plus matching that fills all slots at once.
2. Fix the F4/F5/workload conflict.
3. Offers only after approval, with requirements locked.
4. A per-org approval policy.
5. `git init`, `DESIGN.md`, and a `CLAUDE.md` with a scope cut line.

After that, human-readable IDs and profile switching give the biggest CLI win for the least effort.

Which of these do you want to adopt? And is something else writing the scaffold right now?

## Crew Selection Process

The Astronaut Office assigns the crew that gives the mission the best chance of meeting its objectives, taking into account many factors, including the background and expertise of the astronauts, such as test pilot experience, development work on specific programs, and availability.

The astronauts must be unassigned to other missions, available for flights (for example, by not being on parental leave or on a military assignment), not in a management position precluding their participation, among other requirements.

## Role of the Chief of Astronaut Office

The chief of the astronaut office is a prestigious job historically responsible for selecting the initial crew assignment for each mission, though the chief isn't eligible to fly in space themselves.

The chief is responsible for managing astronaut resources and operations and will help develop astronaut flight crew operation concepts and make crew assignments for future spaceflight missions.

The crew selection process considers multiple factors beyond just technical qualifications, including specific training in particular programs and mission-specific considerations like lunar training for surface missions.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about the Artemis II backup crew astronauts, their roles, and training:

## Backup Crew Members

NASA astronaut Andre Douglas and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jenni Gibbons trained with the crew and served as their backups.

## Backup Role and Purpose

Backup astronauts are trained to replace members of the prime crew in the event that something happens and one of them is unable to complete the mission. Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jenni Gibbons was assigned as CSA astronaut Jeremy Hansen's backup, ensuring that had Jeremy been unable to fly, Canada would keep its seat on this mission.

## Training Requirements

Backup astronauts undergo the same training as the prime crew knowing that they may not get to fly on the mission they are training for, which makes the backup role a unique challenge. They are typically trained in a similar way to be prepared to take on the same duties and responsibilities, sometimes with very little advanced notice.

## Training Locations and Content

The Artemis II crew primarily trains at NASA's Johnson Space Center where there is an Orion simulator, a mock-up of the crew module as well as rocket and spacecraft hardware, and also train at NASA's Kennedy Space Center on launch pad and countdown operations. The backup crew's role involves rigorous training that closely mirrors the primary mission, including familiarizing themselves with Orion systems, emergency procedures, and conducting simulations in simulated space environments.

## Additional Responsibilities

While they did not fly on the mission, they each had their own duties before and through the mission beyond serving as backups to help ensure success.

Based on my web search results, here's what I found about NASA's astronaut crew health stabilization program, quarantine procedures, and post-flight rehabilitation:

## Pre-Launch Quarantine

Current HSP protocols for U.S. launches include a 14 day quarantine period, intended to isolate crew for approximately twice the incubation period of most pathogens of concern. Quarantine involves isolating astronauts for a specific period before launch with contact limited to only close family and launch support personnel who are similarly subject to health stabilization requirements.

Astronauts undergo comprehensive health stabilization processes including contact isolation, thorough medical examinations, immunizations, and a regimen of diet and exercise. Once quarantine begins, astronauts continue to get daily electronic-based medical screening.

## Post-Flight Rehabilitation (45 Days)

Postflight reconditioning begins on landing day, is scheduled for two hours per day, 7 days a week for 45 days and is tailored to the specific needs of the astronaut. Astronauts have 2 hrs/day of protected rehabilitation time for the first 45 days, during which time rehabilitation interruptions must be approved by medical operations.

The postflight reconditioning program is designed to stress the body systems that affect aerobic capacity, muscular strength, power, endurance, stamina, bone, balance, agility, coordination, orthostatic tolerances, proprioception, neurovestibular function and flexibility. Most crew members reached or exceeded their preflight test values 45 days after flight.

Based on the search results, here's information about ISS crew assignment and the Multilateral Crew Operations Panel:

## Multilateral Crew Operations Panel (MCOP) Role

The Multilateral Coordination Board (MCB) has charged the Multilateral Crew Operations Panel (MCOP) with defining the processes, standards and criteria for selection, assignment, training, and certification of Space Station crew for flight.

## International Partners

Crew assignment decisions are made in consensus by the Multilateral Crew Operations Panel (MCOP), comprising representatives from all five international partners: US space agency NASA, Russian space agency Roscosmos, Japanese space agency JAXA, the European Space Agency ESA and the Canadian Space Agency CSA.

## Crew Assignment Process

The Multilateral Crew Operations Panel decides who flies to the International Space Station, and also the high-level functions of crew members on mission, including the ISS commander and which crew members will train for spacewalks and robotic activities. All of these decisions are made in consensus.

Assigning a crew well in advance of a mission is important to ensure crew members have enough time to carry out mission-specific training and are able to work alongside one another on Earth before tackling challenges together in space.

## Crew Standards

The ISS partners have released a document setting out the principles for selecting and assigning astronauts to missions to the ISS. The ISS Crew Criteria Document defines the processes and criteria for selection, assignment, training, and certification of ISS crewmembers.

# Astronaut Mission Assignment Process

**Who Proposes & Decides:**
Each international partner (NASA, Roscosmos, JAXA, ESA, CSA) can nominate personnel through the Multilateral Crew Operations Panel (MCOP), which makes final decisions by consensus.

**Timing:**
"Assigning a crew well in advance of a mission is important to ensure crew members have enough time to carry out mission-specific training."

**Selection Criteria:**
Candidates must satisfy five requirements: general suitability, medical fitness, behavioral suitability, linguistic ability, and adherence to the ISS Code of Conduct. Assessment includes "past and present conduct, interpersonal and communication skills, operational experience and performance under stress."

**Role Assignment:**
The MCOP determines "high-level functions of crew members on mission," including the ISS commander and which astronauts train for spacewalks and robotic activities.

**Backup Crew:**
"The prime crew, who fly to the Space Station, and the backup crew, who train alongside them ready to step up if needed, are usually selected at the same time."

**Mission Preparation:**
Following selection, planning and training commence immediately.

content.text:
I've finished the research: how real crew assignment works, and your decisions checked against it. My take follows, with sources at the end.

## How real missions do it, mapped to our design

- **Picking the crew.** NASA's Astronaut Office picks the crew that gives the mission the best chance of meeting its objectives. It weighs expertise, specific training and availability. Candidates must be unassigned to other missions and available (not on leave, for example). → These are our hard filters.
- **Approval can be a group decision.** On ISS missions a panel from all five partner agencies decides by consensus who flies, and *what role* each person has: commander, spacewalks, robotics. → Missions have named **roles**, and approval can need more than one approver.
- **Backups are real.** The prime crew and the backup crew are usually selected at the same time, and backups train alongside the prime crew (Artemis II had two backups). → Your backup idea is realistic.
- **Crews are assigned well in advance** so they can train and work together before flying. → This is where I push back on hiding teammates (section 3h).
- **Recovery time.** There's a 14-day quarantine before launch and 45 days of reconditioning after landing. → This is where a "rest gap" between missions comes from.
- **One deliberate difference:** space agencies *assign* crew rather than *offer*. For a platform serving private companies, labs and contractors, offer/accept is the right model. State that choice in the doc.

Your flow, grounded in the above:
```
DRAFT      lead defines roles, runs matcher dry-runs, picks nominees (primary + backup per role)
           nominees are PROPOSED: invisible to crew
SUBMITTED  roster frozen, snapshot saved (roster + scores + elimination counts)
APPROVED   approval policy satisfied → PROPOSED becomes OFFERED automatically
           crew accept/decline; gaps → promote backup or top-up match
ACTIVE     all primary roles accepted → crew locked, roster revealed to crew
COMPLETED
```
This answers "what does the director approve?": the plan **and** the named crew.

---

## 1. Matching: the problem, and why your rule is right

**The problem.** A mission needs one Pilot (Nav ≥4) and one Engineer (EVA ≥3).
- A: Nav 5, EVA 4 → qualifies for **both** roles.
- B: Nav 4, no EVA → Pilot only.

A simple greedy engine goes role by role and takes the best person each time:
1. Pilot: A is best → A.
2. Engineer: A is taken, and B doesn't qualify → **empty**. The mission can't be staffed.

The correct answer is B as Pilot and A as Engineer, which fills both. The mistake is choosing the Pilot without checking who the Engineer role could use.

**Your rule** ("if they're about equal, use the less versatile person and keep the versatile one free; if one is clearly better, use the better one") is exactly the right instinct. Written as rules for the engine, in priority order:
1. **Fill as many roles as possible.** A full crew that's slightly weaker beats a strong crew with a gap, since a mission can't go active with an empty role.
2. **Then maximise quality.**
3. **Protect rare people, but only when candidates are close.** Take up to 5 points (out of 100) off anyone whose rare skills this role doesn't need.
   - Pilot role: A scores 88 but holds a rare EVA-4 → effective 83. C scores 86 and has nothing rare → 86. **C gets the seat and A stays free.**
   - If A scored 95 → effective 90, so A still wins. That's your "much, much superior" case.
   - To measure "rare": for each expert-level skill the person holds that this role doesn't need, add 1 ÷ (number of org crew with that skill at that level). Cap it at 1. The match output then explains: *"Kept A free: holds 1 of 2 EVA-4 qualifications."*

**How the engine finds the best combination:** use the **Hungarian algorithm**, the textbook "assign people to seats" method. Turn each role into seats (headcount 2 means 2 seats) and give each person–seat pair a value:
`1,000,000 if eligible + score×100 − rarity×500`
It returns the combination with the most seats filled, then the best total. It's deterministic and instant at this size, and in the interview you can call it "maximum-weight bipartite matching". Backups come from a second run with the primaries excluded.

Make both examples above (Pilot/Engineer, and A vs C) **unit tests**, and use them as the new worked example in the doc. The current example contradicts the data model.

Optimising across *several* missions at once is v2. The rarity penalty is the cheap stand-in for it.

---

## 2. Workload, explained properly

```
                  Oct                Nov                 Dec           Jan
Mission X:                  |==== Nov 1–30 ====|
Crew A:      [= Oct 5–25 =]                                          just back
Crew B:                                            [=== Dec 20 – Jan 30 ===]
Crew C:      (nothing)
Crew D:                           [Nov 10–20]                        overlaps X
```

**What the current design does:**
- Filter F4 removes D, because D is already booked inside November. That's correct: nobody can fly two missions at once.
- The workload score only counts mission days **inside Nov 1–30**. A, B and C all have zero there; anyone with days there was removed like D. So all three score 1.0, and the 25% weight adds the same amount to everyone. **It changes nothing.**
- The "≤2 concurrent missions" cap means "overlapping missions", and F4 already guarantees zero overlap. **It can never trigger.**

Yet A just landed, B is leaving again soon, and C is fresh. The fix is to look *around* the mission, not only inside it:

1. **Keep "no overlap" as a hard rule.** Delete the concurrent-missions cap.
2. **Add a rest gap:** a hard rule, set per org (default 14 days, based on the quarantine period).
   - A's last mission ends Oct 25, and X starts Nov 1: a 6-day gap. **Excluded**, with the reason shown ("rest gap 6d < 14d").
   - B's gap is 20 days → passes.
3. **Measure workload over a wider window**, 90 days either side of the mission (210 days here):
   - B has 42 committed days → workload = 1 − 42/210 = **0.80**.
   - C has none → **1.00**. C ranks above B, so work spreads fairly.

"Committed" means accepted primary and backup seats. Pending offers don't count, but they're flagged in the match output.

---

## 3. Your decisions, one by one

**a. Offers only after approval: agree.** Add a PROPOSED status for nominees, so the approver signs off on named people. This matches the real process, and it also fixes the orphaned-offer problem (offers pointing at requirement rows that got replaced).

**b. Cancellation: agree, with three details.**
- **Who can cancel:** before approval, the owning lead or a director. After approval (APPROVED or ACTIVE), **directors only**, because scrapping an approved mission is a policy decision. A reason is always required.
- **What happens, in one transaction:** proposed and offered seats become WITHDRAWN, accepted seats become RELEASED, and each is tagged with "mission cancelled". Crew see *"MSN-4 'Europa Survey' was cancelled"* in `mc inbox`.
- **Wording:** say "cancelled", not "compromised", which sounds like a security incident.

No notifications table is needed for v1; the inbox can be built from assignment status plus the reason. An email/webhook system is v2.

**c. Backups: good idea, and real.** Build a lean version:
- Each assignment is either PRIMARY or BACKUP. Backups are nominated and approved with the roster, and the offer reads *"Backup for Pilot on MSN-4"*.
- Backups **never** count toward filling a role, so a role can't be overfilled.
- If a primary drops out, the lead runs `mc missions promote-backup` and the backup takes the seat. No re-approval, since backups were already approved.
- Your "backup tells us if they get a primary seat elsewhere": **automate it.** If a backup accepts a primary seat on an overlapping mission, their backup seat is released automatically and the lead sees it in their inbox.
- **Verdict:** build this *after* the core happy path works. Add the PRIMARY/BACKUP column to the schema now either way.

**d. Several offers and double booking: mostly agree, with one simplification.**
- **Crew can hold several pending offers.** Fine.
- **The server checks conflicts when crew accept.** If they've already accepted an overlapping mission, the accept fails with: *"Conflicts with MSN-7 (Nov 3–20). To take this instead: `mc offers withdraw <id>`, then accept."*
  - That gives you "drop the old one to take the new one" with **no new feature**, because withdraw and accept already exist. A one-step `--replace` is v2.
- **Keep the blocked offer, but tell the other lead.** Their `mc missions show` says *"candidate has a conflicting commitment"*, so they can backfill instead of waiting.
- **Switching counts as a dropout on the first mission.** It's logged, it feeds the commitment score, and it triggers backup promotion there.
- **Expiry: yes, as a deadline rather than "±7 days".**
  - Deadline = offered + 7 days, but never later than 14 days before launch. The 7 days is an org setting.
  - Check it when the offer is read; no background job needed.
  - An expired offer carries no penalty, and the lead's inbox shows the role as open again.

**e. Approval: a clarification.** I meant approval **processes**; the brief says orgs have "different… approval processes". That means *who* approves and *how many* approvals are needed, not message text. Two settings per org:
- `approverRoles`: directors only, or directors plus leads.
- `requiredApprovals`: 1 or 2.
- **Always on:** nobody approves a mission they created, directors included.
- Any single rejection rejects the mission. Approvals reset when it's resubmitted.
- Store decisions in a `mission_approvals` table (mission, round, approver, decision, note). It replaces the `approved_by` column.
- **Seed data:** Astra = a director or another lead, 1 approval (your D5). Lunar = directors only, 2 approvals (seed 2 directors).
- This also gives directors a real settings command: `mc org settings set …`.

Your "title line, no full mission brief" call is right. A note on each approve/reject decision is enough.

**f. Self-rating plus lead rating: not over-engineering** if you keep it to two columns:
- `self_rating`, set by crew; `verified_rating`, set by leads or directors, plus who verified it and when.
- The matcher uses the verified rating, and falls back to the self-rating with "⚠ unverified" shown.
- This matches reality: agencies certify their crew; crew don't certify themselves.
- Certification expiry is a nice domain touch, but v2.

**g. Reliability → "commitment".** Only count dropouts *after accepting*. Declines, expiries and cancellations don't count.
- Formula: `(accepts − dropouts + 2) / (accepts + 2)`
  - New crew: 1.0.
  - 1 dropout out of 1 accept: 0.67, not 0.
  - 1 out of 10: 0.92.
- Suggested weights: skill 45%, workload 25%, experience 20%, commitment 10%.
- Define "experience" as completed missions where the person held a role using any of this role's skills, capped at 5.

**h. Crew visibility: partial pushback.** Your instinct is right for *selection* and wrong for *after it*. Real crews are chosen together and train together for months, and compatibility is itself a selection criterion. A customer would find "you meet your crewmates at launch" strange. My rule:
- **Before the crew is locked:** crew see only their own offer (mission, dates, role, primary or backup). They never see who else was offered, declined, ranked or scored.
- **Once ACTIVE** (all primaries accepted): assigned crew see the confirmed roster, names and roles only.
- **Crew never see scores**, their own included. Scores invite gaming and disputes.

"Reveal at ACTIVE" is essentially your "before take-off", and it's a single condition in code.

**i. Tenancy constraints in the database, the pure-function matcher, and rules as data: agreed.** One detail: every child table gets `org_id`, and relations point at `(org_id, id)`.

---

## 4. What to build, what to push, what to cut

**Must build (in this order):**
1. **Roles model:** `mission_roles(name, headcount)` plus `role_skill_requirements(role, skill, min)`. Assignments point at a role.
2. **Matcher as a pure function:**
   - hard filters: role skills, availability, no overlap, rest gap;
   - score: skill, experience, wide-window workload, commitment;
   - Hungarian seat assignment with the rarity penalty;
   - backups;
   - elimination counts, near misses ("3 crew have EVA 3") and "why not X".
3. **Mission lifecycle** as in the flow above, plus a lead withdrawing a submission (SUBMITTED → DRAFT) and cancel with a reason.
4. **Assignment states:** PROPOSED → OFFERED → ACCEPTED / DECLINED / EXPIRED, then WITHDRAWN or RELEASED. The conflict check runs on accept.
5. **Per-org approval policy** (2 settings), the `mission_approvals` table, no self-approval, and a director settings command.
6. **Tenancy:** `org_id` everywhere, composite foreign keys, hashed tokens, and tests that try foreign IDs in request bodies.
7. **Rules as data:** a transition table and a permission map, which also produce `allowedActions` in API responses.
8. **The visibility rules** from 3h.
9. **CLI:** readable IDs (`MSN-12`), profile switching (`mc use lead-astra`), `mc inbox`, `mc missions show` listing the actions available to you, and `match --explain`.
10. **Tests:** the matcher (including both examples from section 1), lifecycle transitions, the role-by-endpoint permission matrix, tenancy, and one end-to-end run.
11. **Repo:** `git init`, `DESIGN.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, a demo script.

**Build if the core is working:** backups (promote, auto-release), offer expiry, self vs verified ratings.

**Push to v2 (write it up in the doc, don't build):**
- **Launch slips after approval:** re-check accepted crew, reopen roles that now conflict, and skip re-approval unless the roles change. This is the most common real-world event and a strong interview topic. It replaces the current "amend" flow.
- One-step offer switching (`--replace`).
- Email/webhook notifications.
- Certification expiry.
- Per-org scoring weights.
- Optimising across several missions at once.
- A direct-assignment mode for agencies that don't use offers.
- "Must/must-not fly together" pairing rules.
- Users in several orgs, and SSO.

**Cut:**
- The "≤2 concurrent" cap (it can't trigger).
- The APPROVED → DRAFT amend flow: the most complexity for the least value. In v1, cancel and recreate.
- Decline-based reliability.
- The manual "backup tells us" step (now automated).
- Separate approval message or brief content.

**Scope warning:** the must list sits at the top of your 5-hour budget. The "build if the core is working" items are your buffer, so tell the other system that order explicitly.

**Your uncommitted `schema.prisma` needs these changes:**
- Add roles, approvals, `org_id` on every child table and composite foreign keys.
- Assignment gains PRIMARY/BACKUP, PROPOSED/EXPIRED/RELEASED statuses, a reason, a `role_id` and an expiry date.
- Split skill ratings into self and verified.
- Add a per-org sequence for readable IDs, and hash the tokens.
- Drop `approved_by`.

The HTML also needs sections 4, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 17 and 18 rewritten to match.

# Mission Control

Multi-tenant crew assignment platform for space organisations — API + CLI.
See [DESIGN.md](./DESIGN.md) for the full design document (data model, lifecycle,
matching engine, decision log).

## Prerequisites

- Node.js ≥ 20
- npm

## Setup

```bash
npm install
cp .env.example .env        # Windows cmd: copy .env.example .env
npm run migrate             # creates SQLite DB and applies migrations
npm run seed                # loads two demo organisations, prints API tokens
```

## Run

```bash
npm run dev                 # API on http://127.0.0.1:3000 (watch mode)
```

Health check: `curl http://127.0.0.1:3000/v1/health`

## Test

```bash
npm test                    # vitest: unit + integration
npm run typecheck           # tsc --noEmit
```

## Seeded demo data

Two organisations — **Astra Dynamics** and **Lunar Collective** — each with a
director, two mission leads, eight crew members, a distinct skill taxonomy,
availability windows, assignment history, and missions in every lifecycle state.
`npm run seed` prints every user's API token.

## Project layout

```
prisma/         schema, migrations, seed
src/
  server.ts     API entrypoint
tests/          vitest suites
DESIGN.md       design document (read this first)
```
import Fastify from 'fastify';
import { PrismaClient } from '@prisma/client';

const prisma = new PrismaClient();
const app = Fastify({ logger: true });

app.get('/v1/health', async () => {
  await prisma.$queryRaw`SELECT 1`;
  return { status: 'ok' };
});

const port = Number(process.env.PORT ?? 3000);

try {
  await app.listen({ port, host: '127.0.0.1' });
} catch (error) {
  app.log.error(error);
  process.exit(1);
}

# Mission Control — Design Document

**Status:** Approved for implementation · **Date:** 2026-09-28 · **Audience:** Engineering team / AI coding agent

> Multi-tenant crew assignment platform for space organisations.

## 1. Problem Statement

Space organisations plan missions that require specific crew capabilities. Assignment today is manual and error-prone: mission leads cross-reference skill profiles, availability calendars, and existing commitments by hand. Multiple organisations will use this platform, each with different crew sizes, skill taxonomies, and approval processes.

**Mission Control** is the core of a multi-tenant B2B platform that lets an organisation manage its crew (skills, availability, history), plan missions with explicit skill requirements and timelines, get *explainable* crew suggestions from an auto-matching engine, move missions through an approval-gated lifecycle, and let crew respond to assignment offers — all exposed through a versioned API and a CLI, with strict tenant isolation and role-based access control enforced server-side.

## 2. Goals & Non-Goals

**Goals**

- Multi-tenant API with three roles (Director, Mission Lead, Crew Member), RBAC enforced server-side on every request.
- Mission lifecycle with an approval gate before activation, including rejection and amendment loops.
- Crew management: per-organisation skill taxonomy, proficiency ratings, availability windows, assignment history.
- Deterministic, explainable auto-matching engine (hard filters → weighted scoring → ranked suggestions with per-criterion breakdown).
- CLI through which every primary workflow can be exercised end-to-end.
- Seed data for two organisations proving tenant isolation and per-org taxonomies.
- Automated tests for the matcher, state machine, permissions, and cross-tenant isolation.

**Non-Goals (explicitly deferred)**

- Web interface (not required by brief).
- Notifications/email delivery — the CLI *is* the crew's inbox (`mc offers list`).
- Multi-org user memberships (a user belongs to exactly one org in this slice).
- OAuth/SSO, token rotation, password flows — seeded API tokens only.
- Equipment/resource constraints, configurable per-org approval chains — designed for, not built (see §17).

## 3. Tech Stack

| Layer | Choice | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Language | TypeScript (Node 20+) | One language across API + CLI; shared domain types; discriminated unions make lifecycle transitions compile-time safe. |
| API framework | Fastify | Typed, fast, schema-first validation via zod; minimal ceremony. |
| ORM / DB | Prisma 6 + SQLite | Zero-infra local run (submission requirement); datasource swap to Postgres/Cloud SQL is the documented production path. |
| CLI | Commander | Standard, testable, subcommand tree mirrors the API. |
| Validation | zod | Single source of request schemas. |
| Tests | Vitest | Fast, TS-native, runs unit + integration against a throwaway SQLite file. |
| Packaging | Single npm package, `src/` by module | No monorepo overhead at this size; clear module boundaries instead. |

## 4. Decision Log

**D1 — TypeScript end-to-end.** API and CLI share domain types (mission status unions, DTOs). Lifecycle states are a discriminated union with exhaustive `switch` handling, so adding a state without handling it fails compilation. *Rejected:* Python — equally viable, but splits the type system between CLI and API and diverges from the hirer's primary stack.

**D2 — Per-organisation skill taxonomy via relational tables.** `skills` is org-scoped (each org defines its own taxonomy — a hard brief requirement). Proficiency lives on the `crew_skills` join (1–5). Mission demand lives on `mission_skill_requirements` (min proficiency + headcount). The matcher is plain SQL over indexed tables. *Rejected:* fixed skill enum (breaks per-org taxonomies); JSON blob on crew (unqueryable, no referential integrity, unindexable for matching).

**D3 — Single `users` table with hierarchical role enum.** `role ∈ {DIRECTOR, MISSION_LEAD, CREW_MEMBER}`, one per user per org. Hierarchy: DIRECTOR ⊃ MISSION_LEAD ⊃ CREW_MEMBER — permission checks ask "is role ≥ X". Crew-specific data lives in satellite tables keyed by `user_id`. *Rejected:* separate crew/lead/director tables — duplicates columns, complicates auth, makes inheritance awkward. A standalone `roles` lookup table adds a join for zero benefit over an enum at this size.

**D4 — Token auth; org always server-derived.** Seeded API tokens map to (user, org, role). Every request resolves the token; the org scope comes from the token, **never** from a client-supplied `orgId`. A crew member with only a token can act through the CLI with zero risk of cross-tenant leakage — no email/SSO system needed. *Production hardening (documented, not built):* hash tokens at rest, expiry, rotation, per-token scopes.

**D5 — Approval = Director OR non-creator Mission Lead.** The brief states leads "should not be able to approve their own missions" — read as separation of duties: leads *can* approve, never their own. Directors can approve anything. This ambiguity is intentional per the brief; the interpretation is recorded here. *Rejected:* directors-only approval — makes the brief's clause meaningless and creates a single-person bottleneck.

**D6 — Deterministic, explainable matcher over black-box ranking.** Hard filters in SQL, then a documented weighted score with per-criterion breakdown stored on every offer. A lead can always answer "why was I suggested / why not". Deterministic = testable = reviewable. *Rejected:* ML/embeddings — unjustifiable at this data scale, untestable in the time budget, and unexplainable to a customer.

**D7 — Slot-level repair, not mission-level restart.** A crew dropout after approval does **not** re-open the mission. The vacated slot is backfilled by top-up matching while the mission stays APPROVED/ACTIVE. Only material changes (dates, requirements) force re-approval via the amendment flow. Least disruption is the design goal.

// Mission Control — data model (design v2)
//
// Tenancy rule: every tenant-owned table carries org_id, and every relation
// between tenant-owned rows is a composite foreign key on (org_id, id). A row
// can only ever reference rows in its own organisation — enforced by the
// database, not by convention. Services additionally scope every query by the
// caller's org (see src/services), so isolation holds on reads and writes.
//
// Dates: mission windows and unavailability are date-only values stored as
// UTC midnight; ranges are inclusive on both ends (see src/lib/dates.ts).

datasource db {
  provider = "sqlite"
  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")
}

generator client {
  provider = "prisma-client-js"
}

enum Role {
  DIRECTOR
  MISSION_LEAD
  CREW_MEMBER
}

enum MissionStatus {
  DRAFT
  SUBMITTED
  REJECTED
  APPROVED
  ACTIVE
  COMPLETED
  CANCELLED
}

enum AssignmentKind {
  PRIMARY
  BACKUP // schema-ready; backup nomination is on TODO.md
}

enum AssignmentStatus {
  PROPOSED // nominated while the mission is a draft — invisible to crew
  OFFERED // sent to crew (on approval, or as a post-approval backfill)
  ACCEPTED
  DECLINED
  EXPIRED // offer passed its respond-by deadline
  WITHDRAWN // retracted before acceptance (lead retracted, or mission cancelled)
  RELEASED // freed after acceptance through no fault of the crew (mission cancelled)
  DROPPED // crew withdrew after accepting — the only status that lowers commitment
}

enum SubmissionDecision {
  PENDING
  APPROVED
  REJECTED
  CANCELLED
}

model Organization {
  id           String   @id @default(cuid())
  name         String
  slug         String   @unique
  keyPrefix    String   @unique @map("key_prefix") // mission keys read AST-12
  missionSeq   Int      @default(0) @map("mission_seq")
  restGapDays  Int      @default(14) @map("rest_gap_days") // min days between two missions
  offerTtlDays Int      @default(7) @map("offer_ttl_days") // days crew have to respond
  createdAt    DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")

  users    User[]
  skills   Skill[]
  missions Mission[]

  @@map("organizations")
}

model User {
  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
  orgId     String   @map("org_id")
  handle    String // short CLI handle, unique per org
  name      String
  email     String
  role      Role
  tokenHash String   @unique @map("token_hash") // sha256 of the API token; plaintext is never stored
  createdAt DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")

  org            Organization        @relation(fields: [orgId], references: [id])
  skills         CrewSkill[]
  unavailability Unavailability[]
  assignments    Assignment[]
  ownedMissions  Mission[]           @relation("MissionOwner")
  submissions    MissionSubmission[] @relation("Submitter")
  decisions      MissionSubmission[] @relation("Decider")
  events         MissionEvent[]

  @@unique([orgId, id])
  @@unique([orgId, handle])
  @@unique([orgId, email])
  @@map("users")
}

model Skill {
  id          String  @id @default(cuid())
  orgId       String  @map("org_id")
  key         String // short CLI handle, e.g. "nav"
  name        String
  description String?

  org          Organization           @relation(fields: [orgId], references: [id])
  holders      CrewSkill[]
  requirements RoleSkillRequirement[]

  @@unique([orgId, id])
  @@unique([orgId, key])
  @@unique([orgId, name])
  @@map("skills")
}

model CrewSkill {
  orgId       String   @map("org_id")
  userId      String   @map("user_id")
  skillId     String   @map("skill_id")
  proficiency Int // 1–5, self-rated by the crew member (lead verification: TODO.md)
  updatedAt   DateTime @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  user  User  @relation(fields: [orgId, userId], references: [orgId, id], onDelete: Cascade)
  skill Skill @relation(fields: [orgId, skillId], references: [orgId, id])

  @@id([userId, skillId])
  @@index([orgId, skillId, proficiency])
  @@map("crew_skills")
}

model Unavailability {
  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
  orgId     String   @map("org_id")
  userId    String   @map("user_id")
  startDate DateTime @map("start_date")
  endDate   DateTime @map("end_date")
  note      String? // private: shown to the crew member and directors only
  createdAt DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")

  user User @relation(fields: [orgId, userId], references: [orgId, id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@index([orgId, userId, startDate])
  @@map("unavailability")
}

model Mission {
  id           String        @id @default(cuid())
  orgId        String        @map("org_id")
  number       Int // per-org sequence; key = <org.keyPrefix>-<number>
  title        String
  description  String?
  startDate    DateTime      @map("start_date")
  endDate      DateTime      @map("end_date")
  status       MissionStatus @default(DRAFT)
  ownerId      String        @map("owner_id")
  cancelReason String?       @map("cancel_reason")
  createdAt    DateTime      @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt    DateTime      @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  org         Organization        @relation(fields: [orgId], references: [id])
  owner       User                @relation("MissionOwner", fields: [orgId, ownerId], references: [orgId, id])
  roles       MissionRole[]
  assignments Assignment[]
  submissions MissionSubmission[]
  events      MissionEvent[]

  @@unique([orgId, id])
  @@unique([orgId, number])
  @@index([orgId, status])
  @@map("missions")
}

model MissionRole {
  id        String @id @default(cuid())
  orgId     String @map("org_id")
  missionId String @map("mission_id")
  name      String // "Pilot", "Flight Engineer"
  headcount Int
  position  Int // display order

  mission      Mission                @relation(fields: [orgId, missionId], references: [orgId, id], onDelete: Cascade)
  requirements RoleSkillRequirement[]
  assignments  Assignment[]

  @@unique([orgId, id])
  @@unique([orgId, missionId, id])
  @@unique([missionId, name])
  @@map("mission_roles")
}

model RoleSkillRequirement {
  orgId          String @map("org_id")
  roleId         String @map("role_id")
  skillId        String @map("skill_id")
  minProficiency Int    @map("min_proficiency")

  role  MissionRole @relation(fields: [orgId, roleId], references: [orgId, id], onDelete: Cascade)
  skill Skill       @relation(fields: [orgId, skillId], references: [orgId, id])

  @@id([roleId, skillId])
  @@map("role_skill_requirements")
}

model Assignment {
  id             String           @id @default(cuid())
  orgId          String           @map("org_id")
  missionId      String           @map("mission_id")
  roleId         String           @map("role_id")
  userId         String           @map("user_id")
  kind           AssignmentKind   @default(PRIMARY)
  status         AssignmentStatus @default(PROPOSED)
  score          Float // matcher score (0–100) at nomination/offer time
  scoreBreakdown Json             @map("score_breakdown")
  reason         String? // decline / drop-out / retraction / cancellation reason
  createdAt      DateTime         @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  offeredAt      DateTime?        @map("offered_at")
  expiresAt      DateTime?        @map("expires_at")
  respondedAt    DateTime?        @map("responded_at")
  closedAt       DateTime?        @map("closed_at")
  updatedAt      DateTime         @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  mission Mission     @relation(fields: [orgId, missionId], references: [orgId, id])
  // (org, mission, role): the role must belong to this mission, in this org.
  role    MissionRole @relation(fields: [orgId, missionId, roleId], references: [orgId, missionId, id])
  user    User        @relation(fields: [orgId, userId], references: [orgId, id])

  @@index([orgId, missionId, status])
  @@index([orgId, userId, status])
  @@map("assignments")
}

model MissionSubmission {
  id            String             @id @default(cuid())
  orgId         String             @map("org_id")
  missionId     String             @map("mission_id")
  round         Int
  submittedById String             @map("submitted_by_id")
  submittedAt   DateTime           @default(now()) @map("submitted_at")
  snapshot      Json // the plan + nominated crew exactly as the director reviewed it
  decision      SubmissionDecision @default(PENDING)
  decidedById   String?            @map("decided_by_id")
  decidedAt     DateTime?          @map("decided_at")
  note          String?

  mission     Mission @relation(fields: [orgId, missionId], references: [orgId, id])
  submittedBy User    @relation("Submitter", fields: [orgId, submittedById], references: [orgId, id])
  decidedBy   User?   @relation("Decider", fields: [orgId, decidedById], references: [orgId, id])

  @@unique([missionId, round])
  @@map("mission_submissions")
}

model MissionEvent {
  id         String         @id @default(cuid())
  orgId      String         @map("org_id")
  missionId  String         @map("mission_id")
  actorId    String?        @map("actor_id") // null = system (e.g. offer expiry)
  type       String // see src/domain/events.ts
  fromStatus MissionStatus? @map("from_status")
  toStatus   MissionStatus? @map("to_status")
  payload    Json           @default("{}")
  createdAt  DateTime       @default(now()) @map("created_at")

  mission Mission @relation(fields: [orgId, missionId], references: [orgId, id])
  actor   User?   @relation(fields: [orgId, actorId], references: [orgId, id])

  @@index([orgId, missionId, createdAt])
  @@map("mission_events")
}

  orgId     String   @map("org_id")
  handle    String // short CLI handle, unique per org
  name      String
  email     String
  role      Role
  tokenHash String   @unique @map("token_hash") // sha256 of the API token; plaintext is never stored
  createdAt DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")

  org            Organization        @relation(fields: [orgId], references: [id])
  skills         CrewSkill[]
  unavailability Unavailability[]
  assignments    Assignment[]
  ownedMissions  Mission[]           @relation("MissionOwner")
  submissions    MissionSubmission[] @relation("Submitter")
  decisions      MissionSubmission[] @relation("Decider")
  events         MissionEvent[]

  @@unique([orgId, id])
  @@unique([orgId, handle])
  @@unique([orgId, email])
  @@map("users")
}

model Skill {
  id          String  @id @default(cuid())
  orgId       String  @map("org_id")
  key         String // short CLI handle, e.g. "nav"
  name        String
  description String?

  org          Organization           @relation(fields: [orgId], references: [id])
  holders      CrewSkill[]
  requirements RoleSkillRequirement[]

  @@unique([orgId, id])
  @@unique([orgId, key])
  @@unique([orgId, name])
  @@map("skills")
}

model CrewSkill {
  orgId       String   @map("org_id")
  userId      String   @map("user_id")
  skillId     String   @map("skill_id")
  proficiency Int // 1–5, self-rated by the crew member (lead verification: TODO.md)
  updatedAt   DateTime @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  user  User  @relation(fields: [orgId, userId], references: [orgId, id], onDelete: Cascade)
  skill Skill @relation(fields: [orgId, skillId], references: [orgId, id])

  @@id([userId, skillId])
  @@index([orgId, skillId, proficiency])
  @@map("crew_skills")
}

model Unavailability {
  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
  orgId     String   @map("org_id")
  userId    String   @map("user_id")
  startDate DateTime @map("start_date")
  endDate   DateTime @map("end_date")
  note      String? // private: shown to the crew member and directors only
  createdAt DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")

  user User @relation(fields: [orgId, userId], references: [orgId, id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@index([orgId, userId, startDate])
  @@map("unavailability")
}

model Mission {
  id           String        @id @default(cuid())
  orgId        String        @map("org_id")
  number       Int // per-org sequence; key = <org.keyPrefix>-<number>
  title        String
  description  String?
  startDate    DateTime      @map("start_date")
  endDate      DateTime      @map("end_date")
  status       MissionStatus @default(DRAFT)
  ownerId      String        @map("owner_id")
  cancelReason String?       @map("cancel_reason")
  createdAt    DateTime      @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt    DateTime      @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  org         Organization        @relation(fields: [orgId], references: [id])
  owner       User                @relation("MissionOwner", fields: [orgId, ownerId], references: [orgId, id])
  roles       MissionRole[]
  assignments Assignment[]
  submissions MissionSubmission[]
  events      MissionEvent[]

  @@unique([orgId, id])
  @@unique([orgId, number])
  @@index([orgId, status])
  @@map("missions")
}

model MissionRole {
  id        String @id @default(cuid())
  orgId     String @map("org_id")
  missionId String @map("mission_id")
  name      String // "Pilot", "Flight Engineer"
  headcount Int
  position  Int // display order

  mission      Mission                @relation(fields: [orgId, missionId], references: [orgId, id], onDelete: Cascade)
  requirements RoleSkillRequirement[]
  assignments  Assignment[]

  @@unique([orgId, id])
  @@unique([orgId, missionId, id])
  @@unique([missionId, name])
  @@map("mission_roles")
}

model RoleSkillRequirement {
  orgId          String @map("org_id")
  roleId         String @map("role_id")
  skillId        String @map("skill_id")
  minProficiency Int    @map("min_proficiency")

  role  MissionRole @relation(fields: [orgId, roleId], references: [orgId, id], onDelete: Cascade)
  skill Skill       @relation(fields: [orgId, skillId], references: [orgId, id])

  @@id([roleId, skillId])
  @@map("role_skill_requirements")
}

model Assignment {
  id             String           @id @default(cuid())
  orgId          String           @map("org_id")
  missionId      String           @map("mission_id")
  roleId         String           @map("role_id")
  userId         String           @map("user_id")
  kind           AssignmentKind   @default(PRIMARY)
  status         AssignmentStatus @default(PROPOSED)
  score          Float // matcher score (0–100) at nomination/offer time
  scoreBreakdown Json             @map("score_breakdown")
  reason         String? // decline / drop-out / retraction / cancellation reason
  createdAt      DateTime         @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  offeredAt      DateTime?        @map("offered_at")
  expiresAt      DateTime?        @map("expires_at")
  respondedAt    DateTime?        @map("responded_at")
  closedAt       DateTime?        @map("closed_at")
  updatedAt      DateTime         @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  mission Mission     @relation(fields: [orgId, missionId], references: [orgId, id])
  // (org, mission, role): the role must belong to this mission, in this org.
  role    MissionRole @relation(fields: [orgId, missionId, roleId], references: [orgId, missionId, id])
  user    User        @relation(fields: [orgId, userId], references: [orgId, id])

  @@index([orgId, missionId, status])
  @@index([orgId, userId, status])
  @@map("assignments")
}

model MissionSubmission {
  id            String             @id @default(cuid())
  orgId         String             @map("org_id")
  missionId     String             @map("mission_id")
  round         Int
  submittedById String             @map("submitted_by_id")
  submittedAt   DateTime           @default(now()) @map("submitted_at")
  snapshot      Json // the plan + nominated crew exactly as the director reviewed it
  decision      SubmissionDecision @default(PENDING)
  decidedById   String?            @map("decided_by_id")
  decidedAt     DateTime?          @map("decided_at")
  note          String?

  mission     Mission @relation(fields: [orgId, missionId], references: [orgId, id])
  submittedBy User    @relation("Submitter", fields: [orgId, submittedById], references: [orgId, id])
  decidedBy   User?   @relation("Decider", fields: [orgId, decidedById], references: [orgId, id])

  @@unique([missionId, round])
  @@map("mission_submissions")
}

model MissionEvent {
  id         String         @id @default(cuid())
  orgId      String         @map("org_id")
  missionId  String         @map("mission_id")
  actorId    String?        @map("actor_id") // null = system (e.g. offer expiry)
  type       String // see src/domain/events.ts
  fromStatus MissionStatus? @map("from_status")
  toStatus   MissionStatus? @map("to_status")
  payload    Json           @default("{}")
  createdAt  DateTime       @default(now()) @map("created_at")

  mission Mission @relation(fields: [orgId, missionId], references: [orgId, id])
  actor   User?   @relation(fields: [orgId, actorId], references: [orgId, id])

  @@index([orgId, missionId, createdAt])
  @@map("mission_events")
}
